nodes.name: NiFe LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe LDH was grown on NF (2 cm × 3 cm) via a hydrothermal process. An aqueous solution containing 0.7 mmol Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 2.1 mmol Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 4 mmol NH₄F, and 10 mmol urea was transferred to a Teflon-lined autoclave along with NF and heated at 120 °C for 6 h. After cooling to room temperature, the NiFe LDH/NF was rinsed with deionized water, dried at 60 °C. The loading mass of NiFe LDH is 1.93 mg cm⁻².

nodes.name: CoFe LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH was prepared on NF (2 cm × 3 cm) by dissolving 3 mmol Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 1 mmol Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, and 3 mmol urea in 30 mL deionized water. This mixture and the nickel foam substrate were placed in a Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 120 °C for 6 h. After cooling, the CoFe LDH/NF was thoroughly rinsed, dried at 60 °C. The loading mass of CoFe LDH is 1.59 mg cm⁻².

nodes.name: PF₆⁻ Intercalation
nodes.procedure: NiFe LDH/NF electrode was held at 1.15 V for 10 min in PF₆⁻-containing seawater to obtain PF₆⁻-intercalated NiFe LDH/NF, with Hg/HgO and graphite serving as reference and counter electrodes, respectively. The sample was then removed, rinsed with deionized water, dried at 60 °C.

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in PF₆⁻-containing alkaline seawater (scan rate 10 mV/s)
nodes.source_text: A standard three-electrode configuration was employed to evaluate the OER performance of NiFe LDH/NF in alkaline seawater, either containing 20 mM PF₆⁻ or without any additive. As shown in the polarization curves (Fig. 1a, Supplementary Fig. 6), the presence of PF₆⁻ reduces the overpotentials required to obtain the j of 200, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻² (209, 247, 282 mV) ... Faradaic efficiency for oxygen evolution at 1 A cm⁻² reaches nearly 100% ... operates stably for over 5000 h ... over 2300 h

nodes.source_text: The NiFe LDH/NF||Pt/C/NF electrolyzer requires only 2.02 V to achieve a j of 1.0 A cm⁻². Furthermore, the energy consumption at the j of 0.2 and 0.5 A cm⁻² is calculated to be 3.60 and 4.04 kWh m⁻³ H₂ ... maintain stable performance for over 1000 h at a j of 1.0 A cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns verify successful synthesis of NiFe LDH/NF with Ni:Fe ~3:1 and confirm PF₆⁻ intercalation by interlayer spacing expansion (Supplementary Figs. 1–5, 15–19).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extensive characterizations via X-ray diffraction (XRD), ... verify the successful synthesis of NiFe LDH/NF with a Ni:Fe atomic ratio of ~3:1 (Supplementary Figs. 1–5, Supplementary Table 1)... Structural analyses, including XRD, SEM, TEM, HRTEM, and HAADF-STEM (Supplementary Figs. 15–19), collectively confirm the successful incorporation of PF₆⁻ into the NiFe LDH interlayers.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals 2D nanosheet array morphology of NiFe LDH/NF on nickel foam and confirms structural preservation after 120 h testing with PF₆⁻ (Supplementary Figs. 26, 27).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface and structural morphologies were examined via scanning electron microscopy (SEM) on a Gemini SEM 300 (ZEISS)... Morphological characterizations reveal that NiFe LDH/NF in PF₆⁻-containing seawater preserves its NF skeleton and 2D nanosheet arrays, while the PF₆⁻-free electrode suffers severe structural failure after 120 hours (Supplementary Figs. 26, 27).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and HRTEM verify nanosheet structure of NiFe LDH/NF and confirm PF₆⁻ intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-resolution TEM (HRTEM)... verify the successful synthesis... Structural analyses, including... TEM, HRTEM... confirm the successful incorporation of PF₆⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM verifies NiFe LDH/NF structure and PF₆⁻ intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-angle annular dark field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) verify the successful synthesis... Structural analyses, including... HAADF-STEM, collectively confirm the successful incorporation of PF₆⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS quantifies 5.93 wt% P in PF₆⁻-intercalated NiFe LDH (Supplementary Table 4) and shows Fe leaching reduced from 1.5 μg mL⁻¹ to 0.291 μg mL⁻¹ and retained Fe increased from 14.5 μg cm⁻² to 263.5 μg cm⁻² with PF₆⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses also confirm the successful incorporation of PF₆⁻, quantified at 5.93 wt.% by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS; Supplementary Table 4)... The Fe concentration leached from NiFe LDH/NF in PF₆⁻-containing seawater is notably lower (0.291 μg mL⁻¹) compared to PF₆⁻-free seawater (1.5 μg mL⁻¹). Correspondingly, the Fe retained... is markedly higher (263.5 μg cm⁻² vs. 14.5 μg cm⁻²; Supplementary Fig. 25).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms PF₆⁻ incorporation with distinct P 2p and F 1s peaks (Supplementary Fig. 23a,b); Ni 2p shifts to lower binding energies, Fe 2p to higher binding energies (Supplementary Fig. 23c,d). Also confirms PF₆⁻ incorporation in CoFe LDH (Supplementary Fig. 32).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses also confirm the successful incorporation of PF₆⁻, ... with distinct P 2p and F 1s peaks (Supplementary Fig. 23a, b), alongside shifts toward lower and higher binding energies for Ni 2p and Fe 2p, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 23c, d)... Operando Raman spectra... with additional evidence from XPS P 2p and F 1s spectra supporting PF₆⁻ incorporation (Supplementary Fig. 32).

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES reveals reduced oxidation state for Ni and elevated oxidation state for Fe after PF₆⁻ intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analyses... revealing a reduced oxidation state for Ni and elevated oxidation state for Fe after PF₆⁻ intercalation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows Ni–OH/Ni–O peaks at 454/527 cm⁻¹ transforming to NiOOH peaks at 475/556 cm⁻¹, with PF₆⁻ E_g vibration indicating intercalation and surface accumulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Raman spectroscopy... In PF₆⁻-free seawater, Raman spectra... show peaks at 454 and 527 cm⁻¹... two additional peaks emerge at 475 and 556 cm⁻¹... an additional E_g vibration of PF₆⁻ is observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS confirms abundant PF₆⁻, Fe retention, and minimal Cl⁻ on PF₆⁻-intercalated NiFe LDH after 120-h test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) further confirms the retention of Fe, abundant PF₆⁻, and minimal Cl⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms presence of P, F, Ni, Fe, and O throughout NiFe LDH nanosheets after long-term test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping and XPS analyses... conducted after the long-term test confirm the presence of P, F, Ni, Fe, and O throughout the nanosheets.
